source_snapshot.procedure: Authenticated Redfish GET of `/redfish/v1/Chassis/Flyboy_Sensor/Thermal`, then check the response.
source_snapshot.criteria: Response data are readable, correct and error-free.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek substitutes IPMI CPU power sensors for the required Redfish CPU temperature resource and exposes credentials in command arguments.

original_test_intent.purpose: Read the target AMD server's CPU temperature data from the specified BMC Redfish Thermal resource and verify that the returned CPU readings are readable, correctly identified and valid for the current platform and operating context.
original_test_intent.target: CPU temperature sensor entries exposed by the verified BMC at `/redfish/v1/Chassis/Flyboy_Sensor/Thermal`; not host CPU power, DIMM power or generic IPMI SDR output.
original_test_intent.scope: One authenticated read of the source URI and validation of every CPU temperature entry in that response. It does not set thresholds, fan policy, workload, power or any thermal control.
original_test_intent.operation: Discover/verify the BMC and resource identity, perform one protected HTTPS GET, preserve HTTP and full JSON evidence, map CPU temperature members to CPU/socket topology and compare their reading/unit/state/health and any published thresholds with the approved platform definition.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 5 attended and 5 machine minutes and specifies one response check, not continuous polling or a stress interval.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The GET succeeds with a valid Redfish JSON payload; required CPU temperature sensors are present, uniquely mapped, readable in the schema-defined unit, report valid state/health and meet the owner-approved current-context rules without response errors.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: BMC/SUT/AMD CPU/firmware identity, exact URI and resource type/version, timestamp/load context, HTTP status/headers, complete redacted JSON, CPU topology and sensor mapping, per-sensor reading/unit/state/health/available thresholds, platform comparison and no-write audit.
ambiguities: The product-specific CPU sensor list, mapping and acceptable readings are absent.
The source curl syntax contains a space after `https://`, embeds credentials in the URL and disables certificate verification.
The source does not state whether `Flyboy_Sensor` is stable across firmware versions.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly restores Redfish temperature semantics, full JSON, CPU mapping and read-only safety. However, it calls the complete requested activity fully automatable while simultaneously requiring an unavailable vendor URI/schema, CPU mapping and range package. Under V3 that obtainable but missing acceptance package belongs in REQUIRES, while Actual Value collection remains safe.

applicable_history.decision: V2 correctly rejects the unrelated DeepSeek CPU-power/IPMI command. No user decision supplies the missing Flyboy sensor map or expected CPU range for this exact firmware.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: The read itself is fully machine-executable and safe, but completion of the source's `data are correct` criterion requires the firmware-specific CPU sensor mapping and acceptance rules. Reclassify to REQUIRES without blocking read-only Actual Value collection.

available_now: The target vendor URI, GET operation and temperature intent are stated.
After protected access is available, complete Actual Value JSON can be collected without the missing expected-value package.
missing_inputs: The BMC/AMD platform owner must provide the supported firmware/URI mapping, required CPU sensor members, CPU/socket associations and acceptable state/health/range semantics for the current load and ambient context.
The automation owner must provide a schema-aware Redfish client/parser with trusted certificate handling and secret-safe session or header authentication.
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The BMC/AMD platform owner supplies the sensor map and expected rules; the automation/security owner supplies the approved client, trust store and protected authentication path.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Verify service-root, Chassis and Thermal resource identity and capture the complete redacted GET response, HTTP status and schema metadata.
List candidate CPU temperature members and record Actual Values, state/health and related-item links without declaring PASS.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not use the DeepSeek CPU-power/IPMI command, embed credentials in the URL, use `-k` without an approved exception, change thermal controls, clear logs, invent missing thresholds or declare correct/PASS before owner mapping.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Confirm the exact firmware supports the source URI, validate parser/resource version, map every required CPU sensor to topology, and compare captured values/status against the approved context-dependent rules.

revision_candidate.test_name: AMD CPU Temperature through BMC Redfish Thermal Resource
revision_candidate.purpose: Read and validate CPU temperature data from the specified BMC Redfish Thermal resource without changing workload or thermal controls.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The AMD server and BMC firmware for which `Chassis/Flyboy_Sensor/Thermal` is the owner-approved resource, using protected Redfish access and a schema-aware client.
revision_candidate.target_scope: All CPU temperature sensor entries in one complete response from the verified source URI. CPU/DIMM power sensors, host-only tools, continuous monitoring and thermal-policy testing are outside scope.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Verified identities/versions; protected credentials and TLS trust; approved Redfish client/parser; firmware-specific resource/schema; required CPU sensor-to-socket map; current load/ambient context; owner acceptance rules; protected evidence storage.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Verify the service and exact resource, then perform one authenticated HTTPS GET using a session token or protected header rather than URL credentials. Preserve HTTP status and complete redacted JSON. Parse all CPU temperature members, mapping each to the correct CPU/socket and recording reading, unit, state, health, optional thresholds and related links. Compare with the owner rules; issue no write.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct BMC/SUT/AMD CPU and firmware verified; URI supported; certificate policy and credentials approved; schema/mapping available for final verdict; load/ambient context recorded; no concurrent firmware update.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Identity/version/timestamp/context; exact URI and resource type; HTTP status/headers; complete redacted JSON; required-versus-observed CPU sensor inventory; per-sensor topology mapping, reading/unit/state/health and available thresholds; comparison; errors/missing fields; no-write audit.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The target firmware's owner-approved sensor map and range/status rules, interpreted with DMTF Redfish Data Model DSP0268 2025.3 for Thermal temperature fields. The legacy Chassis Thermal URI remains applicable only because this product source explicitly names it; DSP2046 2025.2 marks that URI deprecated for new implementations, not invalid for compatible existing products.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: GET/read only. Do not expose credentials/tokens, bypass certificate validation without an approved exception, alter fan/threshold/power/workload state, clear logs, substitute IPMI power data or fabricate absent schema members.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: No interactive approval for authorized read-only collection. The platform owner must supply/approve sensor mapping and expected-value rules before a final PASS/FAIL verdict.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Automation can collect, parse and compare a supplied map. The AMD/BMC engineer judges firmware-specific sensor identity and whether readings are correct for the recorded load/ambient context.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No target recovery is expected. On wrong resource, TLS/authentication failure, malformed JSON, missing mapping or invalid sensor data, preserve evidence and stop interpretation; correct inputs before one bounded reread.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Wrong target/firmware; unsupported URI; certificate or credential exposure; non-success HTTP status; schema mismatch; malformed/truncated response; CPU member cannot be mapped; invalid unit/state/reading; missing expected rules for final verdict; or any proposed thermal write.

identified_defects: DeepSeek tests CPU power through IPMI instead of CPU temperature through Redfish.
Source authentication syntax leaks credentials and disables TLS verification.
The platform CPU sensor map and acceptable-value rules are missing.
V2's FULLY classification conflicts with its own dependency on an unavailable vendor acceptance package.
reason_for_change: Keep the safe Redfish Actual Value path available, but classify the complete correctness judgment according to its missing product-specific schema/map/range package and remove the unrelated CPU-power path.

new_technical_evidence.title: Redfish Data Model Specification
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Redfish Thermal temperature members, subject to the target firmware's implemented schema
new_technical_evidence.supports: Thermal temperature examples use ReadingCelsius, Status, PhysicalContext and RelatedItem to represent and associate CPU readings.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The target's vendor resource membership and accepted values are not defined.

new_technical_evidence.title: Redfish Resource and Schema Guide
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Current schema guidance and backward-compatible legacy Thermal resources
new_technical_evidence.supports: The Chassis/{ChassisId}/Thermal URI is deprecated in favor of ThermalSubsystem for new implementations, but remains documented for compatibility; this row must use its explicit vendor URI rather than silently migrate.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The exact Redfish schema version implemented by Flyboy firmware is unknown.

new_technical_evidence.title: Redfish Specification
new_technical_evidence.supports: Redfish supports Basic and session authentication over HTTPS; session tokens provide a protected alternative to URL-embedded credentials.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The lab trust-store and chosen authentication method are not supplied.

removed_ambiguities: Separates CPU temperature from CPU/DIMM power.
Defines one GET rather than indefinite monitoring.
Separates safe Actual Value collection from final correctness judgment.
resolved_blockers: The absent expected range does not prevent complete read-only collection of current CPU temperature evidence.
remaining_blockers: Final correctness judgment requires the exact firmware sensor map and owner-approved context-dependent rules.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 reconciles capability with the missing vendor acceptance package, preserves the exact legacy vendor URI without treating deprecation as invalidity, and explicitly allows Actual Value collection while withholding PASS.
